clips.text: roots
A basil plant has dry soil. Which part takes in water when we water the soil? A. Roots B. Flowers
Roots take in water from soil.
A young tomato plant is watered at its roots. Which part carries water upward? A. Stem B. Fruit
The stem supports the plant and carries water.
compare
Two matching seedlings have the same water and soil. Only the light direction changes. What are we testing? A. A response to light B. A response to different pots
Change only the light direction to investigate this response.
A lamp moves to the right of a young shoot. What is a reasonable prediction over time? A. It may grow toward the light. B. It instantly jumps into the lamp.
Many young shoots gradually grow toward light.
backbone
A dolphin swims, but it has a backbone. Which group fits? A. Vertebrate B. Invertebrate
A backbone is evidence for the vertebrate group.
A snail crawls and has no backbone. Which group fits? A. Vertebrate B. Invertebrate
A snail is an invertebrate.
life cycle
A caterpillar stops feeding and forms a pupa. What can come next? A. An adult butterfly B. A frog egg
An adult butterfly can emerge from the pupa.
A tadpole has growing legs and a shrinking tail. What stage is it approaching? A. Froglet B. Butterfly pupa
It is developing toward a froglet.
evidence
Same cups, soil amounts, water, and time. A drains 40 mL; B drains 15 mL. Which drains more? A. A B. B
40 mL is more than 15 mL under these test conditions.
Same conditions. C drains 18 mL; D drains 48 mL. Which drains less? A. C B. D
18 mL is less than 48 mL.
observe
You see a rock photo. Can you measure its actual mass from this picture alone? A. No. We need a suitable measuring tool. B. Yes. A darker color tells its mass.
A photo alone does not measure actual mass.
Two real stones look similar. How could you compare how rough they feel? A. Touch their surfaces carefully. B. Guess from the names.
Touch provides evidence about how a surface feels.
trace
A rock preserves a trail of footprints. What is supported? A. An animal moved there. B. We know its exact skin color.
Footprints record activity, but not exact skin color.
A leaf shape is preserved in rock. What can you observe directly? A. The outline of the leaf B. The exact smell of the living plant
The preserved outline is visible evidence.
older
In undisturbed layers, shell rock is below leaf rock. Which was deposited first? A. Shell layer B. Leaf layer
The lower layer was deposited first in this undisturbed sequence.
Fish fossils occur above a lower shell layer. The layers are not overturned. Which layer is younger? A. Fish layer B. Shell layer
The upper layer is younger in this sequence.
reuse
A clean, sturdy box can hold craft supplies. Which action is reuse? A. Use it for storage. B. Buy a new box and throw this one away.
Reusing an item can reduce the need for a new one.
A notebook still has blank pages. What reduces paper waste? A. Use the blank pages. B. Throw it away now.
Use the remaining pages before buying another notebook.
resource
A wooden spoon and a paper bag can both begin with which resource? A. Trees B. Coal only
Wood and much paper come from trees.
Many conventional plastic bottles use raw materials from which resource? A. Petroleum B. Wool
Petroleum supplies raw materials for many conventional plastics.
speed
Both carts travel for 6 seconds. A goes 12 units, B goes 18. Which has greater average speed? A. A B. B
For the same time, B travels farther.
Both carts travel 24 units. A takes 4 seconds, B takes 8. Which has greater average speed? A. A B. B
For the same distance, A takes less time.
predict
A cart goes beyond the station. Keep the track and cart fixed. What could you test next? A. Earlier braking B. Change every condition
Earlier braking is a relevant change to test.
A cart stops before the station. What is a useful prediction to test? A. Later braking may bring it closer. B. Its color must make it stop early.
Test a relevant change and compare the result.
attract
A classroom magnet lifts iron nails but not aluminum pieces. What can it separate here? A. Iron from aluminum B. Every kind of plastic
Use the observed magnetic response to separate these materials.
Two magnet ends marked N face each other. What should happen? A. Repel B. Attract
Like poles repel. Unlike poles attract.
pitch
Keep vibration size the same. Change from 250 to 500 vibrations per second. What changes? A. Pitch becomes higher. B. Gravity disappears.
Faster vibrations produce a higher pitch.
Keep vibration frequency fixed, but make the vibration larger. What changes in this model? A. The tone gets louder. B. The pitch must get lower.
A larger vibration amplitude increases this tone’s loudness.
Roots take in water and minerals from the soil.
A blank supports the plant and carries water. stem. seed coat
A stem supports the plant and carries water.
If the light moves, the young shoot may grow toward it.
I keep water and soil the blank when testing light. same. opposite
I keep water and soil the same when testing light.
A frog has a backbone, so it is a vertebrate.
A snail has no backbone, so it is an blank. invertebrate. vertebrate
A snail has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.
A caterpillar becomes a pupa before it develops into an adult butterfly.
A tadpole develops into a blank. froglet. seedling
A tadpole develops into a froglet.
Sample A drains more water than sample B in this test.
For a fair soil test, use the same blank of water. amount. color of cup
For a fair soil test, use the same amount of water.
I observe the surface and use a tool to measure the mass.
I use a blank to compare mass, not just a photograph. balance. lamp
I use a balance to compare mass, not just a photograph.
A footprint is evidence of an animal’s activity in the past.
The fossil does not tell us every blank. detail. clue
The fossil does not tell us every detail.
In undisturbed layers, the lower layer is older.
We need more evidence for an blank age in years. exact. older
We need more evidence for an exact age in years.
Reusing a useful item can reduce the need for new materials.
A loose shelf screw may need blank before reuse. repair. more paint only
A loose shelf screw may need repair before reuse.
Wood can be used for furniture, buildings, and paper.
Coal can be burned to generate blank. electricity. new trees
Coal can be burned to generate electricity.
For the same distance, the faster cart takes less time.
For equal time, compare the blank traveled. distance. color
For equal time, compare the distance traveled.
If I brake earlier, the cart may stop closer to the target.
After testing, I compare my prediction with the blank. result. favorite color
After testing, I compare my prediction with the result.
A magnet attracts iron. It does not attract every metal.
Unlike magnetic poles blank. attract. repel
Unlike magnetic poles attract.
If the vibrations are faster, the sound has a higher pitch.
At the same frequency, larger vibrations make a tone blank. louder. higher in pitch
At the same frequency, larger vibrations make a tone louder.
Compare two fallen leaves. Record their shapes and one visible difference. What can you see? What would require touching?
Watch an animal from a distance. Record an action and separate what you see from what you guess. What is your observation? What is still unknown?
Choose three familiar household objects. Describe their visible materials and how the materials suit the job. Which material is useful for this task? Why?
Look at a shoe print in sand or a photograph of one. Record two visible features. What can the print tell you? What can it not tell you?
Find a clean, safe item that can be reused. Ask an adult before changing its use. What new use did you choose? What new material could it save?
With an adult, use a low cardboard ramp and a toy car. Keep the start and car the same; compare two surfaces. What did you keep the same? Where did the car stop?
Make a gentle humming sound. Notice the vibration at your throat. Try a higher and a lower pitch at comfortable volume. How was higher different from louder?
Move the lamp to one side. Compare how a young shoot may grow toward light over time. This is a simplified model, not a live plant.
Lamp on the left. Over time, the young shoot may bend left toward the lamp.
Lamp on the right. Over time, the young shoot may bend right toward the lamp.
